newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady-off, feeders steady-up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady-off, feeders steady-up.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.200 cent a lb higher, livestock analysts said.

Falling boxed beef prices and concern over larger fed cattle supplies into the summer months were expected to weigh on live cattle futures despite the discount of futures to cash. Previous USDA cattle reports indicated fed cattle supplies would increase in coming months, analysts said.
Futures also look technically set to break further as they near chart points, they said.

Feeder cattle futures will likely be underpinned by another advance in the latest CME feeder cattle index Thursday to a 26-month high. Strong demand for replacement feeders and moderate feed costs as well as recent heavy death losses in the northern plains from storms and flooding should encourage buying interest, analysts said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index climbed $0.39 to $72.54 per cwt, the highest level since February 21, 1995.
